interpretation: The proof combines two categorically different reductions. Algebraically, the chosen mollifier makes the Dirichlet coefficients b(n) of B=LM−1 vanish exactly below M^(1−b) and on square arguments up to M^(2(1−b)). Analytically, Mellin contour decomposition moves the remaining evaluation to controllable lines, fourth-moment and large-sieve estimates bound the boundary pieces, and the character average is rewritten through Dirichlet L-functions: square indices can contribute a pole, whereas nonsquare contributions have no pole and are suppressed by contour shifts and moment bounds rather than annihilated. This exact-cancellation/analytic-suppression split leaves only controlled tails, yields the stated estimates for the first and second moments of B, and hence proves the W estimate and I3 control. Its force depends on the mollifier support and squarefree coefficients, smoothing, zero-free input, and parameter ranges.
